subject: Commit phasing: Orbit AI slab forecast and SLO fit
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel@orbit.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Liu <sarah@orbit.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial traffic profile and ask for Dedicated sizing

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Orbit AI would like to move from the Hosted API to a Dedicated pool for our production recommender generator. We put together a short traffic profile attached (orbitai_prod_profile.csv) — highlights below:  
- Typical steady: 12 requests/sec, ~420 tokens per request (prompt+response)  
- Peak spurts: up to 65 requests/sec lasting 10–30s (concurrent interactive flows)  
- Daily 95th token rate: ~18k tokens/sec, short spikes up to ~27k tokens/sec  
- Target latency SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end generation <= 350 ms for average 420-token responses (user-facing interactive)

We are on a 3-month ramp plan and expect committed TPS to start low and then step up. We'd like Redwood's recommendation for:  
1) Initial slab/GPUs to reserve for month 1 and month 3 (committed)  
2) Burst capacity and fallback model options to meet SLO during spikes  
3) Any ops notes (KV cache, batching knobs, quantization suggestions) that affect headroom numbers

Attached: orbitai_prod_profile.csv (CSV), a short internal doc.

Can we sync briefly next week? Happy to share credentials for a short load test if helpful.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of ML Ops
Orbit AI
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@orbit.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial traffic profile and ask for Dedicated sizing

Daniel — thanks for the profile and the clear SLO target. Quick read-through below and I copied Marissa (Capacity & Sales) and Karthik (Solutions Eng) to confirm ops + recommend slabs. High level first pass:  

- Baseline sizing: to meet a 95th <= 350ms for ~420-token responses at steady 12 req/s (5k tokens/sec), a small 4-GPU slab of A100-80-like instances (or 6x T4-equivalents with quantization) should be fine for month 1 with conservative batching.
- Spike handling: your spike envelope (65 req/s, 420 tokens) -> ~27k tokens/sec. To hit the SLO during those 30s spikes we need burst capacity around 5–6x baseline — roughly a 24 GPU hot pool or access to burst shared capacity.
- Headroom recommendation: reserve capacity for expected committed avg (month 3 target) + 1.5x operational headroom, and enable autoscale/burst to avoid full overprovisioning.

Questions before we lock numbers:  
1) Are responses fully generated in one streaming call (single request) or chunked? Streaming affects per-token latency breakdown.
2) Do you have a preferred quantized model family? Using an int8-quantized variant moves more of the delta into the kernel path and increases tokens/sec per GPU.
3) Any strict data residency / private deploy constraints?

I'll coordinate a short infra calc and a suggested commit phasing plan — Marissa, Karthik: can you weigh in with slab counts + a quick ops playbook (KV cache lifetimes, batch target) and a suggested doc/commit we can send to Orbit?

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel@orbit.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Initial traffic profile and ask for Dedicated sizing — proposed slab phasing

Ava / team — quick slab math and operational notes. Pasting our internal calc (summary):

Assumptions:  
- Model footprint: 7B dense baseline (unquantized) -> ~tokens/sec per A10080: ~3.5k tokens/sec at p95 lat budget; int8 quantized -> ~5.5k tokens/sec (same latency budget).  
- Steady target month1 committed: 5k tokens/sec (your steady ~12 req/s x 420 tokens).  
- Month3 committed target: 12k tokens/sec (expected customer ramp).  

Sizing proposal (committed + burst):
- Month 1 committed: Reserve 2 A10080 GPUs (pool) -> raw ~7k tokens/sec unquantized, gives 1.4x headroom for steady. If Orbit enables int8 quant we can recommend 1 GPU committed (but customers often want buffer).
- Month 3 committed: Reserve 4 A10080 GPUs -> ~14k tokens/sec (fits 12k committed + small headroom).
- Burst capacity: Provide access to a shared burst slab of 20 GPUs for short spikes; configure policy to route to cheaper quantized variants first and escalate to full-reserved when latency degrades.

Operational levers and notes:  
- KV / prefix caching: set TTLs to 3–5m for session-level reuse; can reduce tokens/sec by ~12–18% for repeat context.  
- Batching targets: prefer continuous micro-batching at 8–12ms latency window for high qps to improve GPU utilization.  
- Autoscale policy: two-step — quick burst from shared pool (0–60s cooldown), then warm reserved slabs for 5–15min sustained increases.  
- Fallback model: recommend a smaller quantized 7B as fallback with documented regression checks; add quality gating in the console.

SLA/Commit recommendation:  
- Offer a 3-month commit with month1 = 2 GPUs reserved, month2 = 3 GPUs, month3 = 4 GPUs, plus shared-burst entitlement of up to 20 GPUs (pay-as-you-go when used). Include a clause for documented load tests prior to turning on full burst.

I attached a rough proposal PDF (orchid_commit_proposal_v2.pdf) which you can share as a starting point. Vivek — flag any infra constraints on the shared-burst idea (networking / tenant isolation).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Capacity Planning Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel@orbit.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Initial traffic profile and ask for Dedicated sizing — proposed slab phasing

Quick infra check — shared-burst is feasible but operational caveats:

- Isolation: We'll run burst workloads in their own tenant slice with strict network egress rules. Data plane separation will be enforced via isolated NVMe mounts and per-tenant KMS keys for session keys. Adds ~8–12% latency overhead worst case; include in SLO planning.
- Cold-start penalty: spinning up additional reserved slabs from cold can take 60–120s depending on cloud region; prefer warm-standby for critical windows.
- Monitoring hooks: enable token-level telemetry and a per-slab queue depth metric to trigger circuit-breaker before tail latency climbs.

Operational action items for the proposal doc:
1) Add a paragraph about the expected latency overhead of the shared-burst path and recommended SLO adjustment during burst windows.
2) Add a pre-burst load-test requirement and a signoff step (we'll provide a test harness).
3) Note that quantized fallback should be validated on your evaluation prompts (we can run a 24-hour regression check).

Ava / Marissa: I'll add the infra bullet points to the proposal. Once Daniel confirms we can schedule a short load run (we prefer a 2x sustained run and two short 30s spikes at 1.5–2x expected peak).

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infra Ops
Redwood Inference
